steps.question: Did this call write or change a project file (source, config, tests or docs) by script, instead of the edit, write or patch tools? A project file is one in the project's own tree, such as src/, crates/, packages/, docs/, or a named source or config file like package.json or Cargo.toml. A file downloaded or generated by the same command or session, a file under a run or scratch folder (such as $RUN or /tmp), and a log are not project files. YES: sed -i or perl -pi on a project file, a heredoc or a > or >> redirect into a project file, or a Python or Node script that wrote a project file. NO for everything else. In particular NO for saving a download (curl -o, gh api ... > file); output to a run or scratch folder, a log or /dev/null; tools whose job is to write files (formatters, package managers, git, code generators, builds and tests); file management (mkdir, cp, mv, rm, rsync); and commands that only read or ran programs.

then.text: Chauffeur: Change files with the edit, write, or patch tools, not scripts, heredocs, or redirects. They show the change and keep permission checks working.
